changesApplied.changeMade: Added authentication tables: users (12 fields + 3 indexes), organizations (5 fields + 2 indexes), user_organizations (5 fields + 3 indexes), refresh_tokens (6 fields + 2 indexes)
changesApplied.reason: Schema was missing tables required for user authentication flow. Users created via CLI had nowhere to persist, and login queries returned empty results causing 401 errors.
changesApplied.impactAnalysis: Adds 4 new tables with proper field definitions, data types, indexes, and PERMISSIONS FULL. Enables user persistence and login queries. Backward compatible - existing activity tables unchanged.

changesApplied.changeMade: Fixed query result parsing at line 69. Added logic to handle nested SurrealDB result structure: checks for dict with 'result' key, list of lists, or direct dict. Extracts actual user record from nested structure.
changesApplied.reason: SurrealDB official library returns nested structure [{'result': [...]}] but code was doing user_data = result[0] which got outer dict instead of user record. This caused KeyError on user_data['password_hash'] resulting in 401 Unauthorized.
changesApplied.impactAnalysis: Fixes critical bug preventing all logins. Handles 3 result format cases for robustness. Added debug logging to trace result structure. No breaking changes - backward compatible with all result formats.
changesApplied.linesAfter: 69-107: Nested if/elif logic extracting user_data from result structure

changesApplied.changeMade: Added comprehensive debug logging: login attempt (email), query result type/length, parsed user_id, password verification status, success/failure warnings
changesApplied.reason: Insufficient logging made debugging 401 errors impossible. Need visibility into query results, parsing logic, and password verification to diagnose failures.
changesApplied.impactAnalysis: Adds 8 log statements for debugging. Uses info level for key events, debug for verbose data, warning for failures. No functional changes - pure observability improvement.

changesApplied.reason: SurrealDB record IDs with hyphens cause parse errors: 'Parse error: Unexpected token `-`'. Hyphens need escaping in record IDs but underscores work natively.
changesApplied.impactAnalysis: Fixes user creation failures. All new users will have underscore IDs. Existing users with hyphen IDs (if any) still work - no migration needed. Low risk change affecting only ID format.

changesApplied.changeMade: Added debug logging for password hash generation, record ID, and creation result
changesApplied.reason: Need visibility into user creation process to verify password hashing, record ID format, and successful persistence to database.
changesApplied.impactAnalysis: Adds 4 log statements for debugging. No functional changes - pure observability. Helps diagnose user creation failures.

changesApplied.changeMade: Created bash script to copy schema SQL to RPC API pod and execute via Python using get_surreal_client()
changesApplied.reason: Need automated way to apply schema changes to deployed Kubernetes database without manual SQL execution.
changesApplied.impactAnalysis: DevOps automation script. Safely applies schema with error handling. Can be run multiple times (IF NOT EXISTS guards). No runtime impact.

dataFlowChanges.before: CLI → user_ops.create_user() → bcrypt.hashpw() → db.create('users:user-{uuid}') → [FAILS: parse error]
dataFlowChanges.after: CLI → user_ops.create_user() → bcrypt.hashpw() → db.create('users:user_{uuid}') → SUCCESS → users table
dataFlowChanges.impact: User creation now succeeds. Users persist to database with proper schema.

dataFlowChanges.before: POST /auth/login → db.query('SELECT...') → result[0] → [FAILS: gets dict not user] → KeyError → 401
dataFlowChanges.after: POST /auth/login → db.query('SELECT...') → parse nested result → user_data = result[0]['result'][0] → SUCCESS
dataFlowChanges.impact: Login queries now correctly extract user record from nested result structure.

dataFlowChanges.after: user_data extracted → verify_password(plain, hash) → bcrypt.checkpw() → SUCCESS → JWT token
dataFlowChanges.impact: Password verification now executes and succeeds for correct passwords.

dataFlowChanges.after: Password verified → create_access_token(user_id, email, org_id, role) → JWT → LoginResponse
dataFlowChanges.impact: JWT tokens now generated and returned to dashboard.
